Question:
Tyler has entered a buffet line in which he chooses one kind of meat, two different vegetables and one dessert. If the order of food items is not important, how many different meals might he choose?

Meat: beef, chicken, pork

Vegetables: baked beans, corn, potatoes, tomatoes

Dessert: brownies, chocolate cake, chocolate pudding, ice cream
Solution:
The two vegetables form an unordered pair, so choosing beans and corn gives the same meal as choosing corn and beans. Count each pair using whichever vegetable appears earlier in the menu list: baked beans can be paired with any of the other \(3\) vegetables; corn can be paired with either of the \(2\) later vegetables; and potatoes can be paired with tomatoes in \(1\) way. This includes every pair exactly once, giving
\[
3+2+1=6
\]
vegetable pairs.

For each pair there are \(3\) meat choices and \(4\) dessert choices. These three selections completely determine a meal, so the total is
\[
3\times6\times4=\boxed{72},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
